## What's new in 1.9.1

**Self-update from your own update server**, worldwide, without a public IP.

- **Update server** (`gundil-update-server`, files starting with `server-`): one server tells every Gundil Intercom which version to install, **upgrade or downgrade**, and hands out the files. The apps reach it like internet calls (public Nostr relays, STUN, UDP hole punching), so it runs at home behind CGNAT: on a Linux PC or server, a Raspberry Pi or Orange Pi, an **OpenWrt router**, a **Windows PC** (service) or as an **AppImage**.
  - **Admin web page** (port 8780): one `admin` account only; a **one-time password after a new install that must be changed** at the first sign-in; **signed out after 30 minutes without activity**; locked for 5 minutes after 5 wrong passwords.
  - **Devices** (who runs what, pin one device to a version), **Policy** (per kind of device: the version and Off / Ask / Install automatically), **Versions** (add GitHub releases, keep copies on the server, or upload files), **Server** (the server code, network check, log).
  - **On OpenWrt, a LuCI page** (Services → Gundil update server): status, the server code, a link to the admin page, settings (address, data folder, repository), log, restart and Reset portal.
  - **`deploy.sh user@host`** installs or upgrades it (back end and web page) from your computer over SSH, on Linux, OpenWrt or Windows; `--web-only` copies just the web page. **`gundil-reset-portal`** starts the portal afresh (`--all`, `--new-key`).
- **In the apps: Settings → Updates.** Checks a minute after start and every 6 hours, or *Check now*. Windows installs silently and restarts; the Linux AppImage replaces itself; Android downloads and asks you to tap Install (it can't downgrade); the Mac puts the new zip in Downloads; iPhone shows that an update is there. The headless node and **gundil-gateway** update themselves when the server says *Install automatically*.
  - The apps trust only your server (its **server code**, built in from the repository variable `GUNDIL_UPDATE_SERVER`, or pasted in Settings → Updates). Every file is checked against its SHA-256; it comes from your server, or from the GitHub release when the server keeps no copy.
- **Release files** now start with `app-` (the apps, the node and the gateway) or `server-` (the update server).
- On Linux the gateway now lives in `/opt/gundil-gateway` (so it can update itself); run `sudo ./install.sh` again when upgrading by hand.

Upgrading: install over 1.9.0; settings are kept. Self-update starts with this version: devices on 1.9.0 or older need this one installed by hand.
